name: CIS Linux Benchmark (Distribution Independent) — Level 1
description: Center for Internet Security Distribution Independent Linux Benchmark — Level 1 (essential security hygiene). This is distinct from CIS Controls v8 (organisation-level controls) which uses a different numbering.

controls.name: Address space layout randomization
controls.desc: ASLR randomises memory layout per-process, mitigating memory-corruption exploits.

controls.name: Restrict core dumps from SUID programs
controls.desc: Core dumps from SUID binaries can leak privileged process memory. `fs.suid_dumpable=0` prevents this.

controls.name: SELinux or AppArmor active
controls.desc: Mandatory access control limits damage from compromised services by restricting what processes can access.

controls.name: Security patches applied
controls.desc: Unpatched systems are vulnerable to known exploits. Security updates should be applied promptly.

controls.name: Strong TLS configuration
controls.desc: Weak protocols (SSLv3, TLSv1) and ciphers (RC4, DES) are cryptographically broken and allow eavesdropping.

controls.name: IP forwarding disabled
controls.desc: Prevents the server from routing packets between networks, reducing its attack surface as a pivot point.

controls.name: ICMP redirects rejected
controls.desc: ICMP redirects can be used to alter routing tables in man-in-the-middle attacks.

controls.name: Reverse path filtering
controls.desc: Drops packets with spoofed source addresses, preventing IP spoofing attacks.

controls.name: Firewall active
controls.desc: Host-level packet filtering is the first line of defense against unauthorized network access.

controls.name: Audit daemon active
controls.desc: auditd records security-relevant kernel events for forensic investigation and breach detection.

controls.name: Time synchronization configured
controls.desc: Synchronised clocks are required for correlating logs across hosts and for valid TLS / Kerberos behaviour.

controls.name: SSH password auth disabled
controls.desc: Password-based SSH is vulnerable to brute-force. Key-based authentication is cryptographically stronger.

controls.name: SSH public key auth enabled
controls.desc: Public key authentication provides strong, phishing-resistant login without transmitting secrets.

controls.name: SSH X11 forwarding disabled
controls.desc: X11 forwarding exposes the graphical display over SSH, enabling screen capture and keystroke injection.

controls.name: SSH MaxAuthTries limited
controls.desc: Limiting authentication attempts per connection slows brute-force attacks.

controls.name: SSH root login disabled
controls.desc: Direct root login bypasses audit trails and increases brute-force risk. Use sudo for privilege escalation.

controls.name: No world-writable files
controls.desc: World-writable files in system directories can be modified by any user, enabling configuration tampering.

controls.name: SUID executables audited
controls.desc: SUID binaries run with elevated privileges. Each one is a potential privilege escalation vector.

controls.name: No extra UID 0 accounts
controls.desc: Non-root accounts with UID 0 have full root privileges, bypassing all access controls.

controls.name: Strong password hashing
controls.desc: /etc/shadow must use a modern hash (yescrypt, sha512, argon2). MD5 / SHA-1 hashes are crackable in hours.

controls.name: Shadow file permissions
controls.desc: /etc/shadow contains password hashes and must be readable only by root.
